long_biography.plain_text:
Oceanco gave Theodore P. Angelopoulos control of a specialist manufacturing business beyond commercial shipping. After becoming majority shareholder in 2002, he established the Dutch yard at Alblasserdam and redirected it towards custom vessels above 80 metres. The strategy produced a distinct generation of large builds before Oceanco changed ownership.

Metrostar Management shows Angelopoulos working through repeated asset cycles. He sold a 19-tanker fleet to General Maritime in 2003, then rebuilt the platform through later acquisitions and newbuilding orders. Recent expansion has returned the company to Suezmax and product tankers while adding container ships. That willingness to sell at scale and re-enter selected segments has kept Metrostar active through changing freight markets.

uncertainties.detail: The owner record and Wikipedia metadata give Vlachorrapti, while Wikipedia's prose and the Leadership 100 award biography give Athens. Neither side has sufficiently strong, consistent primary documentation to justify correcting the existing value, so the dossier does not use birthplace in either biography.
Court and maritime records consistently establish the initial P., but no reviewed source expands it. The proposal therefore fills only the verified initial rather than inventing a middle name.

Court findings conclusively establish inter vivos transfers of Alpha Steel and Beta Steel to Theodore. Lloyd's List establishes that he continued part of the family shipping operation after its division, but public sources do not provide a complete allocation schedule for every shipping asset.

Public material refers historically to real estate, private equity and a former UBS position, but no sufficiently current ownership evidence establishes those as principal holdings. The primary-industry classification therefore rests on the active and publicly identifiable Metrostar shipping platform.

Angelopoulos's former majority ownership and strategic shift are well documented, and Oceanco changed ownership in 2010. It is treated as a durable operating episode, not a current holding or a reference to his personal vessel history.

No identity-verifiable personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, Twitter or personal website cleared the acceptance threshold. Metrostar's official domain is proposed only as a Company Website and is independently tied to Angelopoulos's current leadership.

No dedicated Forbes profile was found. Forbes articles identify the exact shipping and steel magnate and document the Metrostar fleet sale, but are retained as reporting rather than mislabelled as a personal profile.

Current personal-vessel associations, spouse's separate career, volatile net-worth estimates, wealth rankings, residence values, disputed birthplace detail and unsupported current investment claims were excluded. Nothing has been compiled or applied.
